cards.issue_title: Maha Super Housing Loan scheme facts live only in More details, not in the product
summary_4_lines: The scheme name and facts for Bank of Maharashtra’s Maha Super Housing Loan are useful: a customer could take them to the branch and say “this is your scheme.”
Those facts sit only in the More details drawer. They said Bank of Maharashtra itself has no answer to “what is your scheme?”
If someone already thinks their loan is under some other scheme, they may never open this dump and never see it.
They said this static bank information should live in the product itself, not as a blog.
cards.pinpoint: On Explore banks, Bank of Maharashtra Maha Super Housing Loan scheme facts (bank, scheme name, facility, purpose, rate type, borrower category) exist only as static content in the More details drawer; they said a customer can take this to the manager as the bank’s scheme, but Bank of Maharashtra itself has no answer, a customer who already thinks they are under a scheme will miss it, and this static information should be out in the product, not a blog.
cards.on_screen_object: More details drawer → Scheme accordion for Bank of Maharashtra · Maha Super Housing Loan
quotes_sample: No, this is definitely good information.
There is no answer in the bank of Maharashtra.
It should be in the product.
related_discussion_one_liners: Super Housing Loan as the named scheme they do not necessarily want — they still need the bank to name its scheme.
Other banks put a page per bank; they will talk about that page later; not as a blog.
Better way to show the money / this is the best way; ASR “draw points are good” as praise of the drawer dump’s points.
More details is good but “not important” relative to putting the same facts in the product.
Continues the previous recording’s More details versus table (vertical vs horizontal); plus/underline/More-about-the-bank cue is a separate problem (issue-02).
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is that Maha Super Housing Loan scheme identity only lives in the More details dump instead of the product, not the table More cue/label and not the loan-amount how-calculated layout.

cards.issue_title: More / plus / underline cue is confusing, and More about Bank of Maharashtra is a little misleading
summary_4_lines: The extra-info control on Bank of Maharashtra is hard to notice: they said the bank did not underline it, they put a clip/plus, and asked how anyone would guess underline.
They said extra info should not be big, not on the phone, and the column should not be big — put a plus sign.
The button reads like more about the bank. They said if you take Maha Super Housing Loan you should know more about the loan.
They called that a little misleading, not standard, and “more and more” if you just write More.
cards.pinpoint: On Explore banks, the extra-info control on the Bank of Maharashtra row (More / clip / plus / possible underline) is hard to guess, and the label More about Bank of Maharashtra is a little misleading because they said a Super Housing Loan customer should know more about the loan, not more about the bank; putting More on the loan amount instead opens calculations, which they treated as a different, clearer job.
cards.on_screen_object: Compare-table Bank of Maharashtra row: More button (accessible name More about Bank of Maharashtra) plus the bank-name / loan-amount underlines that open drawers
quotes_sample: The bank of Maharashtra didn't underline it.
related_discussion_one_liners: ADD.info / plus sign / not big / not on the phone / column not big — brainstorming the cue, still the same issue.
Generally, when people are told what is inside, they click it.
Brief EMI drawer open/close (₹37,938) while comparing which numbers are clickable — related, not a separate EMI issue.
“This is the dump of all information” ties back to issue-01’s static dump, but here the attack is the cue and label.
ASR “solenoid” while they say they used to write more details — quoted raw; likely a mishear of a prior label, not an on-screen solenoid.
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is how extra info is cued and labeled on the Bank of Maharashtra row (More / plus / underline / more about the bank vs the loan), not where scheme facts live and not the loan-amount steps’ neatness.

cards.issue_title: Loan-amount how-calculated drawer is not neat and needs a color code for the min of two
summary_4_lines: They opened how Bank of Maharashtra’s ₹48,00,000 was calculated and said you just follow 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 — the information is great.
They then said it is not just neat: a color code would show the two limits, left-side vs right-side calculation, 1-2-3 then minimum of 2.
They also asked where 240 months is, then mapped it to 20 years on the table.
This walk is unfinished: the next recording starts by arranging the same steps.
cards.pinpoint: On Explore banks, the Bank of Maharashtra loan-amount how-calculated drawer (six steps to ₹48,00,000) is information they like if you follow 1–5, but they said it is not just neat: they want a color code so the two limits show as left-side vs right-side 1-2-3 then minimum of 2, and they had to hunt 240 months against the table’s 20 years.
cards.on_screen_object: Loan amount drawer for Bank of Maharashtra · Maha Super Housing Loan (opened from ₹48,00,000 — Show how loan amount for Bank of Maharashtra was calculated); six numbered steps including 240 months and Lowest of these limits
quotes_sample: If you have a color code, it will show you.
related_discussion_one_liners: Praise: information is great; just follow 1–5; math is correct.
Credit-card hypothetical (“10 lakhs”) while looking at 10.00% load — related walk of step 3, not a separate missing-10-lakh bug.
“I have to pay 14,000” / “what about this? I don't know” while on eligibility vs EMI leftover — same neatness/color problem.
“20% … that's the limit” near the end — related to LTV/limit talk on the same cards.

cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is the loan-amount how-calculated drawer’s neatness, color code, min-of-two limits, and 240 months vs 20 years — not scheme facts living only in More details and not the More/plus/underline bank label.
